==English==

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:der|la:supervivo<alt:supervīvere>}}
From {{der|en|xno|survivre}}, {{der|en|fro|survivre}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|supervivo|supervīvere|t=to outlive}}, from {{der|en|la|super|t=over}} + {{m|la|vivere|t=to live}}, akin to {{m|la|vita|t=life}}. See {{m|en|vivid}}. Compare {{m|en|devive}}, {{m|en|revive}}. Displaced native {{ncog|en|thrive}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/səˈvaɪv/|/səˈvʌɪv/|a=UK}}
* {{IPA|en|/sɚˈvaɪv/|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-survive.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|aɪv|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{sid|en|living}} {{lb|en|intransitive|of a person}} To continue to [[live]]; to remain [[alive]].
#: {{ux|en|Whether by a miracle or by good luck, all twenty passengers '''survived'''.}}
# {{sid|en|existing}} {{lb|en|intransitive|of an object or concept}} To continue to [[exist]].
#: {{ux|en|This town has been hit by two hurricanes, but it '''survives'''.}}
# {{sid|en|live past}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[live]] past (a life-[[threaten]]ing event)
#: {{syn|en|overlive<qq:nonstandard>}}
#: {{ux|en|Whether by a miracle or by good luck, all twenty passengers '''survived''' the crash.}}
#: {{ux|en|He did not '''survive''' the accident.}}
#: {{ux|en|This house has '''survived''' two hurricanes.}}
# {{sid|en|outlive}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[live]] longer than (someone); to [[outlive]] (someone or something); to [[outlast]] (something).
#: {{syn|en|overlive<qq:nonstandard>}}
#: {{ant|en|predecease#Verb}}
#: {{hypo|en|postdecease#Verb}}
#: {{ux|en|His children '''survived''' him.}}
#: {{ux|en|He was '''survived''' by his children.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Taming of the Shrew|II|I|text=And for that dowrie, Ile aſſure her of / Her widdow-hood, be it that ſhe '''ſuruiue''' me / In all my Lands and Leaſes whatſoeuer / Let ſpecialties be therefore drawne betweene vs, / That couenants may be kept on either hand.}}
#* {{RQ:Scott Rob Roy|volume=I|page=227|text=I am afraid, as will happen in other cases, the treaty of alliance has '''survived''' the amicable dispositions in which it had its origin.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=January 22, 2020|author=Stuart Jeffries|title=Terry Jones obituary|url=https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2020/jan/22/terry-jones-obituary|text=Jones is '''survived''' by his second wife, Anna (nee Söderström), whom he married in 2012, and their daughter, Siri; and by Bill and Sally, the children of his first marriage, to Alison Telfer, which ended in divorce.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261015124407/https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2020/jan/22/terry-jones-obituary|archivedate=15 October 2026}}
# {{sid|en|victim}} {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be a victim of nonfatal but substantial harm and nonetheless to display the strength to heal; especially, after a crime or an illness, especially sexual or physical [[abuse]] or [[assault]], [[cancer]]{{,}} or a [[natural disaster]].
#: {{ux|en|I just know you'll get through this, because that's what survivors like you do: they not only '''survive''' but thrive.}}
# {{sid|en|avoid}} {{lb|en|intransitive|sports|of a team}} To [[avoid]] [[relegation]] or [[demotion]] to a lower [[division]] or [[league]].
#: {{ux|en|They narrowly '''survived''', but the heat is on.}}
